title: Spark pins some savings vaults to the Sky Savings Rate and leaves others to bounded discretion
content:
The Rewards Rate configurations split the vault portfolio into two governance regimes. Three are pinned: USDC on Ethereum, USDC on Avalanche and PYUSD "will be maintained to be equal to the Sky Savings Rate" (A.6.1.1.1.3.5.3.2.3.1, .3.4, .3.5). Four are discretionary: USDT on Ethereum, USDG on Robinhood Chain, USDT on Arbitrum and USDT on X Layer are each "set via the vault's setter role... within the Min Yield and Max Yield bounds," and within those bounds "may be set as a fixed value or by reference to an external benchmark" (.3.2, .3.6, .3.7, .3.8).

The definition at A.6.1.1.1.3.5.3.2.1 opens that reference class deliberately wide: "the Sky Savings Rate, **Secured Overnight Funding Rate**, SparkLend market supply rates, or other relevant measures." Naming SOFR is notable — it imports a traditional-finance policy rate into a DeFi governance parameter, so a vault can be priced against dollar funding markets rather than against crypto-native yields.

The split itself tracks strategic intent rather than risk. USDC and PYUSD are assets Sky wants to convert into its own: paying exactly the SSR makes a Spark Savings deposit economically identical to holding sUSDS, which removes any yield reason to prefer the native alternative. USDT vaults, spread across four chains, are a growth and distribution play where the right rate depends on local competition — so they get a band and a human.

The cost of the pin is inflexibility: an SSR-matched vault cannot respond to a competitor outbidding it on a specific chain, and cannot be trimmed if it grows faster than Spark can deploy the inflow. The cost of the band is the one visible throughout this Artifact — the stated rate becomes unknowable from the document, and only the min/max bounds remain authoritative.
description: USDC, PYUSD and Avalanche USDC must equal the SSR exactly, while USDT, USDG and Arbitrum and X Layer USDT may be set at any fixed value or external benchmark within min and max yield.
